newsitem.title: USA: AC-Pacific Intertie at 2,500 MW Fri-Sat; 3,200 Sun.
newsitem.headline: AC-Pacific Intertie at 2,500 MW Fri-Sat; 3,200 Sun.

text.p: Southbound transmissions on Pacific Intertie's AC segment will be capped at 2,500 megawatts (MW) between 0600 and 1800 PDT Friday and Saturday, Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Thursday.
BPA operates the Northwest portion of the Intertie, which links the region's power system to that of California and the Southwest.
The line was previously rated at 2,800 MW during the day on Friday and at 2,000 MW on Saturday and Sunday.
The schedule now calls for AC transmissions on Sunday to return to 3,200 MW, the level at which the 4,800 MW line has been limited since a power outage on August 10.
The restrictions are related to maintenance work by Pacific Gas and Electric Co, which operates AC Intertie lines crossing through its central and northern California service territory.
Meanwhile, restrictions on the DC segment of the Intertie remain in place, with transmissions limited to 1,086 MW through October 15 and to zero between October 15 and 20.
The DC line has a capacity of 3,200 MW, but it had been capped at 2,000 MW since the August 10 outage.
